Maastricht UMC+
Imaging Department
Date: 12 February 2025
Exam: mpMRI Prostate
Clinical indication: PSA 9.6 ng/mL, prior negative biopsy, PI-RADS assessment requested.
FINDINGS: The prostate measures 30.0 mL in volume. T2-weighted imaging demonstrates a focal area of low signal intensity in the peripheral zone of the left base, measuring approximately 8 mm in diameter. This lesion shows restricted diffusion on DWI (b=1400) with corresponding signal drop on the ADC map. Dynamic contrast-enhanced (DCE) sequences reveal early, moderate enhancement within the same region. No evidence of extracapsular extension, seminal vesicle invasion, or suspicious lymphadenopathy is seen.
IMPRESSION: PI-RADS 3 lesion in the left peripheral zone base. Prostate volume 30.0 mL. PSA density 0.32 ng/mL/mL. Clinical T stage cT1c. csPCa predicted probability 0.6599411.

previous_notes.author: Dr. L. Smits (GP)
previous_notes.text: Patient presented with a PSA of 2.2 ng/mL detected on routine screening. Digital rectal examination was unremarkable. Given the elevated PSA for age, a transrectal ultrasound-guided systematic biopsy was arranged for further evaluation. The patient was advised to continue regular follow-up.

previous_notes.author: Dr. L. Smits (GP)
previous_notes.text: Re-evaluation following a significant PSA rise to 9.3 ng/mL. The patient reports no new urinary symptoms and remains asymptomatic. Given the rapid PSA velocity and prior negative biopsy, a repeat MRI-targeted and systematic biopsy was performed. The patient has been referred to urology for specialist assessment of the rising PSA trend.

pathology_report:

Biopsy timepoint 2 (January 2025): The submitted tissue fragments show benign prostatic hyperplasia and chronic prostatitis. No malignant glands are identified. Gleason score 0+0, ISUP grade group 0. No cribriform or intraductal patterns identified. Perineural invasion is absent.
